children: Construction has begun on several factories and investment projects at Al Suwaiq Industrial City in the North Al Batinah governorate of Oman, supporting economic diversification and local added-value objectives.

The city has localised a number of investment projects across various sectors this year, with a total investment value exceeding 1.4 million Omani riyals ($3.12 million) and a total leased area of more than 80,000 square metres (sqm), said Mundhir bin Ali Al Nasseri, Acting Director General of Al Suwaiq Industrial City.
This brings the city’s cumulative investment volume to over OMR 2 million and the total leased area to more than 90,000 sqm, he added.
The projects cover a range of activities, including polyethylene production, industrial oil refining, polymer-modified bitumen, and ceramic tile manufacturing.

Madayn, the state-owned operator of industrial cities in the country, is currently evaluating a number of investment applications, Al Nasseri said. These include projects to manufacture multi-purpose electric motors and generators, soft drinks, cosmetics and hand and foot care products.
Spanning approximately 12.2 million sqm, Al Suwaiq Industrial City is a significant addition to the sultanate’s network of industrial cities.
Madayn has also developed studies to identify investment opportunities aligned with the economic diversification strategy and Oman Vision 2040.

Targeted sectors include petrochemicals, food industries and modern agriculture, energy and supporting technologies, recycling and environmental industries, light and medium industries, pharmaceuticals, technology and innovation, heavy industries, and logistics.

title: Construction starts on investment projects in Oman’s newest industrial city
